datasets.title: Global Sea Surface Temperature
datasets.description: Ocean currents around the world from March 2007 to March 2008, coloured by how warm the surface water is. The warmest water, around 28 to 30 degrees Celsius, forms a wide band along the equator, and the water cools steadily toward the poles, down to about 0 degrees. The pattern changes slowly, warming in the north during the northern summer and in the south during the southern summer.
datasets.colorMeaning: blue = cold (0°C), green = mild, yellow = warm, red = hot (32°C)
datasets.credit: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio

datasets.title: Change in Night Lights 2012–2023
datasets.description: A view of Earth at night, seen from space, showing where city and town lights shine. Most of the land is dark, with bright clusters where people live. From 2012 to 2023 many areas grow brighter and new lights appear, showing where cities and towns have expanded.
datasets.colorMeaning: bright yellow and white = strong night lights, dark = little or no light

datasets.title: Lightning Events Detected from the ISS 2017–2023
datasets.description: Lightning flashes recorded by an instrument on the International Space Station between 2017 and 2023. Each flash appears as a brief bright spot. Flashes come in sudden bursts, mostly over land in the tropics, and jump from place to place as storms form and fade.
datasets.colorMeaning: bright white and blue spots = lightning flashes, dark = no lightning

datasets.title: DYAMOND Global Carbon Dioxide
datasets.description: A computer model of carbon dioxide in Earth's atmosphere. Plumes of carbon dioxide rise from sources on the ground and are carried by the wind, mostly from west to east. Over time the overall amount of carbon dioxide keeps rising.
datasets.colorMeaning: bright yellow and white = more carbon dioxide, dark = less carbon dioxide
